$comment: The only hand-written part of the token catalog. One entry per token whose role the source comment cannot state on its own: either it has no comment, or the comment above it describes a neighbour. `purpose` is the role sentence shown in the catalog; `stability` is alpha unless a token has been deliberately settled.

--ds-color-background.purpose: The page behind everything. Nothing is painted under it.

--ds-color-border.purpose: The line that separates one area from another: dividers, table rules, the edge of a panel. The visible edge of a control is a different job and is under review.

--ds-color-surface.purpose: Anything that sits on the page as its own area: cards, panels, menus, the inside of a field.

--ds-color-surface-hover.purpose: The same area while the pointer is over it, or while it is the active row of a list.

--ds-color-text.purpose: Ordinary reading text on background or surface.

--ds-color-text-secondary.purpose: Text that supports the main text: hints, captions, units. Still has to reach 4.5:1.

--ds-color-disabled.purpose: The fill of a control that cannot be used right now.

--ds-color-text-disabled.purpose: The text of a control that cannot be used right now. It is exempt from the contrast minimum, so never carry meaning by this colour alone.

--ds-color-focus-ring.purpose: The colour of the ring that shows where the keyboard is. It needs 3:1 against whatever it is drawn on.

--ds-state-hover.purpose: The overlay laid over a control while the pointer is on it.

--ds-state-pressed.purpose: The overlay laid over a control while it is being pressed.

--ds-color-primary.purpose: The fill of the one action a screen is asking for: the primary button, and the selected state that follows from it.

--ds-color-primary-hover.purpose: The same fill while the pointer is on it or it is being pressed.

--ds-color-on-primary.purpose: Text and icons drawn on the primary fill.

--ds-color-secondary.purpose: The fill of an action that is present but not the one being asked for. Same hue as the primary: secondary is a job, not a second colour.

--ds-color-secondary-hover.purpose: The secondary fill while the pointer is on it or it is being pressed.

--ds-color-on-secondary.purpose: Text and icons drawn on the secondary fill.

--ds-color-info.purpose: The colour of a message that tells you something, without anything being wrong.

--ds-color-success.purpose: The colour of a message that says something worked.

--ds-color-warning.purpose: The colour of a message that says to be careful.

--ds-color-danger.purpose: The colour of a message that says something failed, and the fill of an action that destroys something.

--ds-color-danger-hover.purpose: The danger fill while the pointer is on it or it is being pressed.

--ds-color-on-status.purpose: Text and icons drawn on a solid status fill: information, success, danger.

--ds-color-on-warning.purpose: Text and icons drawn on the warning fill. It is dark, because the light warning colour cannot carry white text.

--ds-color-emphasis-surface.purpose: An area that should stand out from the page around it, such as a tooltip or an inverted panel.

--ds-color-on-emphasis.purpose: Text and icons drawn on the emphasis area.

--ds-color-info-border.purpose: The edge of the tinted information surface.

--ds-color-success-border.purpose: The edge of the tinted success surface.

--ds-color-warning-border.purpose: The edge of the tinted warning surface.

--ds-color-danger-border.purpose: The edge of the tinted danger surface.

--ds-color-on-selected.purpose: Text and icons drawn on a selected item.

--ds-color-emphasis-border.purpose: The edge of the emphasis area.

--ds-color-neutral.purpose: The colour of a message that carries no status at all.

--ds-color-neutral-surface.purpose: The quiet fill of a control or chip that carries no status: a plain tag, a default button.

--ds-color-neutral-border.purpose: The edge that goes with the quiet neutral fill.

--ds-elevation-overlay.purpose: The shadow under something floating over the page: a menu, a popover, a dialog. It changes between themes, because a shadow reads differently on a dark page.
